angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,064,421 km at 139.58 pc = 0.1 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 7.1641 +/- 0.0102 mas (same row, RUWE 0.88): 139.58 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.53 +/- 0.02 solar radii from Korth et al. 2024, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1408 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024ApJ...971L..28K/abstract): 1,064,421 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.312 +/- 0.009 solar masses from Korth et al. 2024, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1408 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024ApJ...971L..28K/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6117 +/- 31 K from Korth et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1408 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024ApJ...971L..28K/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Korth et al. 2024, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1408 c in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024ApJ...971L..28K/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-1408.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.187, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
